gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-khula: Structural from the first glance, Stencilia leaves generous gaps where its curves end and keeps its tall letters tight. Khula is the quieter half, a modern sans-serif whose curves hold their mouths open and whose tall midsection fills the line.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-krub: Krub has a pronounced x-height and a contemporary look. Stencilia, structural and striking, earns its keep big and brief, while the plain sans underneath lets curves trail off unfinished.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-kufam: Kufam reads like a single neon tube, clean and contemporary. Its bodies dominate each line while ascenders barely show, and that unusual look is the quality that stands out most against Stencilia's structural, lower-contrast heading.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend: Approachable in its outsized lowercase, Lexend gives every curve an open jaw, bent like tubing of one gauge throughout. Stencilia's structural gaps make the contrast.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lexend-deca: Clean and approachable, Lexend Deca looks cut from strips of equal width. Stencilia's structural headings sit above it, and the small capitals beside big lowercase keep the text gentle underneath.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-liter: Striking up top, steady below. Liter draws its strokes with one fixed nib, so the plain sans body, with its tall lowercase and wide mouths on round forms, should move along smoothly under Stencilia over many lines.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-mada: Stencilia brings structural, striking letters with generous gaps at its curve terminals. Mada follows with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close, so giving the heading more size than the text would feel natural.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-martel-sans: Neutral and modern, Martel Sans gives every curve a generous opening and holds a high mean line across each word. Stencilia is the one for striking structure; the plain sans is the one for quiet text.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-matangi: Matangi presses twine-like strokes into a flat surface, with rounded letters left open and no hairlines anywhere. Matangi has a hefty lowercase, so Stencilia's heading may look best a few sizes larger than the plain sans text.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-maven-pro: Maven Pro reads modern and smooth, with a welcoming gap in the c and a high-waisted lowercase. But Stencilia is the structural, striking one, while the sans keeps crossbars as fat as the stems they join.
